ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit is a sinusoidal input source labeled 230 V(rms), with the upper end as the positive input end and the lower end connected to the bottom common wire. The upper input end is connected through series capacitor C1=0.1 μF to the middle node. This middle node is connected through diode D1 to the bottom reference wire, and the direction of D1 in the figure makes it conduct and clamp this node when the middle node is negative relative to the bottom reference point. The middle node then goes through diode D2 to the upper right output end, and the direction of D2 is conducting from left to right. The right output end has capacitor C2=0.1 μF connected in parallel to the bottom reference wire, and output Vo is marked between the upper and lower ends on the right. Reasoning: Take the bottom wire as the reference ground. The input voltage is a 230 V(rms) sine wave, so the input peak value Vp = 230√2. When the input reaches the negative peak, D1 conducts and clamps the middle node at the right end of C1 at about 0 V; at this time, the voltage across C1 from left to right is about -Vp. Then when the input reaches the positive peak, D1 is cut off, and ideal capacitor C1 retains the previous charge, so the middle node voltage rises to Vp - (-Vp) = 2Vp. At this time D2 conducts and charges C2 to this peak value. Since the components are ideal and the output end has no discharge load, C2 maintains this voltage in steady state. So the output amplitude |Vo| = 2Vp = 2 × 230√2 ≈ 650.4 V.
